symbols.name: axis index
symbols.meaning: An index naming one axis of the array, running from 1 to D.
symbols.quote: For an axis $\varsigma$ with $1\le\varsigma\le D$, let $t_\varsigma$ be the length of that axis, the number of values its coordinate takes.

symbols.name: input position
symbols.meaning: A position in the input array X, a tuple with one coordinate along each axis.
symbols.quote: A position in $X$ is a tuple $\mathbf{x}=(x_1,\dots,x_D)$ with $0\le x_\varsigma<t_\varsigma$ for every $\varsigma$, where $x_\varsigma$ is the coordinate along axis $\varsigma$.

symbols.name: output position
symbols.meaning: A position in the output array $\mathcal F X$, with the same bounds as a position in X.
symbols.quote: A position $\mathbf{x}'=(x'_1,\dots,x'_D)$ in the output has the same bounds.

symbols.name: multidimensional transform
symbols.meaning: The map that sends an array X to its multidimensional transform $\mathcal F X$.
symbols.quote: Let $\mathcal F$ denote the multidimensional transform, which sends $X$ to the array $\mathcal F X$ by

relations.quote: A multidimensional transform is a Fourier transform taken over several [transform axes](transform-axis.md) at once, computed by transforming along one axis at a time.
The multidimensional transform $\mathcal F$ is built from the [discrete Fourier transforms](discrete-fourier-transform.md) $F_{t_1},\dots,F_{t_D}$ by [tensor product](tensor-product.md).
Each axis transform is computed by the [radix-two factorization](radix-two-factorization.md) as $\lg t_\varsigma$ levels of butterflies, with multiplications by roots of unity between the levels.

relations.quote: The multidimensional transform is written in the representation of [synthetic polynomial transforms](synthetic-transforms.md).
In this representation, the transform turns roots of unity into [signed cyclic shifts](cyclic-shift.md).
